posts.text:
The Korean War front line crossed the entire peninsula four times in three years before settling almost exactly where it started.

Four maps, one war — a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ June 25, 1950: North Korea invades south across the 38th parallel with Soviet-supplied tanks. The Cold War's first hot war begins.
2/ By September 14, 1950, North Korean forces had pushed South Korean and US troops into a tiny corner around Pusan — the whole peninsula nearly fell in under three months.
3/ Then MacArthur's Inchon landing flipped the war. By November 25, 1950, UN forces had driven almost to the Yalu River on the Chinese border — total victory looked close.
4/ China entered the war that same month with hundreds of thousands of troops, pushing the front back south. Seoul changed hands four times total before the lines stabilized.

5/ The armistice signed July 27, 1953 fixed a line close to the original 38th parallel — roughly 3 years and an estimated 3 million+ deaths later, changing almost nothing on the map, but freezing the peninsula into two states still technically at war.

6/ No peace treaty was ever signed — just an armistice. Today's DMZ is a direct descendant of this war.

Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
